text:
Maya Patel: Quick bench roundup comparing A100 vs H100 on a few open models (llama-2-7b, vicuna-13b, mpt-30b). Posting summary + raw command we ran.

Maya Patel: TL;DR: H100 gives a solid latency and throughput win (1.6-2.1x) in our single-stream tests. Cost per 1M tokens ends up similar-to-slightly-favorable for H100 depending on region pricing and nf4 speedups.

Maya Patel: Command used (single-stream, seq=2048, batch=1, no KV cache):
```
bench_infer --model {llama-2-7b,vicuna-13b,mpt-30b} \\
  --gpu {a100,h100} --precision {fp16,nf4} \\
  --seq 2048 --batch 1 --runs 12 --kernel auto
```

Maya Patel: Median results (12 runs, us-central1):
- LLaMA-2-7B:
  - A100: prefill 125ms, decode p/token 8.5ms, tokens/sec 115, $/1M toks ≈ $7.80
  - H100: prefill 65ms, decode p/token 4.2ms, tokens/sec 240, $/1M toks ≈ $7.65
- Vicuna-13B:
  - A100: prefill 260ms, decode p/token 18ms, tokens/sec 57, $/1M toks ≈ $15.00
  - H100: prefill 150ms, decode p/token 9ms, tokens/sec 110, $/1M toks ≈ $14.80
- MPT-30B:
  - A100: prefill 520ms, decode p/token 45ms, tokens/sec 22, $/1M toks ≈ $40.00
  - H100: prefill 320ms, decode p/token 26ms, tokens/sec 38, $/1M toks ≈ $39.50

Jordan Li: Interesting that H100 looks slightly cheaper for us-central given our cost assumptions (A100 $3.50/hr, H100 $5.75/hr). Numbers will flip region-to-region though. Did you try nf4?

Maya Patel: Yes. Quick nf4 pass for 7B/13B: about +1.6-1.8x tokens/sec on both GPUs, prefill/decode improved proportionally. For 30B nf4 gave ~1.35x on H100 and ~1.25x on A100.

Priya Singh: Any evals on quality after nf4?

Maya Patel: Ran our instruction-following and QA evals:
- LLaMA-2-7B nf4: <1% delta on our composite score (negligible)
- Vicuna-13B nf4: ~1% delta, within noise for most prompts
- MPT-30B nf4: a couple of edge-case failures on formatting and long-step reasoning (~2-4% delta depending on metric).
Recommendation: enable nf4 by default for <=13B, gate 30B+ with targeted evals.

Marco Diaz: Kernel selection notes? Anything surprising p95/p99-wise?

Maya Patel: Observed patterns: 
- H100: CUTLASS + FlashAttention2 kernels showed best tail behavior for decode (fp16 and nf4). Auto selector picked CUTLASS/Flash2 for most shapes.
- A100: Triton-backed fused kernels + cuBLAS performed better on some head-dim configs, and gave tighter p99 for long prefill runs. CUTLASS sometimes regressed on certain matrix shapes on A100.
We left kernel=auto in these runs but forcing per-kernel helps p99 tuning.

Jordan Li: Region variance?

Maya Patel: Yes — region delta is non-trivial for tail latency (host/network + instance fam differences):
- eu-west1 median prefill ~ +10-13% vs us-central1
- asia-east1 median prefill ~ +18-22% vs us-central1
So plan for region-specific SLO buffers.

Priya Singh: For capacity planning: if a product needs sustained 1k tokens/sec for llama-7b, how many GPUs?

Maya Patel: Using measured tokens/sec (median sustained):
- A100 ~115 tps -> raw devices = 8.7 -> 9 GPUs. Add 25% headroom -> recommend pool of 12 A100 GPUs.
- H100 ~240 tps -> raw devices = 4.2 -> 5 GPUs. Add 25% headroom -> recommend pool of 7 H100 GPUs.
Note: with nf4 and batching optimizations you can reduce those counts further; also consider caching hot prefixes.

Marco Diaz: Multi-GPU sharding thoughts?

Maya Patel: For <=30B prefer single-GPU serving with quantization. Sharding across GPUs introduces cross-device comms overhead that hurts latency for single-stream workloads. Use model-sharding for 70B+ or for throughput-batched jobs where latency is less critical.

Jordan Li: Any gotchas / failure modes to watch for?

Maya Patel: A few we hit: 
- Kernel OOM when mixing nf4 + very long prefill (8k+) on H100. Fix: bump allocator limits and enable streaming KV cache.
- Triton kernel selection caused p99 spikes on some Vicuna shapes on A100; forcing a different kernel fixed the tail.
- Small variance in quoted cloud GPU prices between regions can flip the $/1M numbers; keep spot/commit options in the calcs.

infra-bot: perf-report generated -> https://internal.redwood/perf/reports/1750001234-h100-a100-bench (dashboards: latency by model, tokens/sec, cost per region)

Priya Singh: Great write-up. Next steps I suggest: 1) batch runs (batch=4/8) to see batching efficiency delta, 2) p99/p999 long-tail runs with streaming KV enabled, 3) nf4 canary for vicuna-13b on dedicated pool.

Maya Patel: Agree. I'll queue batch experiments and the canary next week. Will post follow-ups with kernel-forcing experiments and p99 graphs. Thanks for the feedback :rocket:
